newsitem.title: EGYPT: Moslem militants kill retired policeman in revenge.
newsitem.headline: Moslem militants kill retired policeman in revenge.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants shot dead a retired police major general in the southern Egyptian town of Ashmouneen on Monday to avenge comrades killed by police at the weekend, security sources said.
They said the gunmen -- believed to be members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) -- stormed the house of Major-General Touni Mohammed Abdel Rahman and killed him.
Abdel Rahman's son Wael is a police captain who was part of a convoy which killed three suspected Gama'a members in Sheikh Saleh Basha village on Saturday, the sources said.

Ashmouneen, site of ancient Pharaonic and Ptolemaic cities, lies about 260 km (163 miles) south of the capital Cairo. The town attracted tourists before Moslem militant groups seeking to overthrow the government began targeting visitors, policemen and Christians in their violent campaign.
Since 1992, the Gama'a and other groups have been trying to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people have died in the political violence and government crackdowns on the militants have largely contained their activities to the southern provinces.
